claims.text: The driver's own trace shows he held position inside the pickup geofence for only 144 seconds, from 13:31:56 to 13:34:20, before cancelling at 13:34:24. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec), so the effective in-geofence dwell falls 36 seconds short of the minimum. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

The shortfall is confirmed by the derived arrival block itself: longest_run_sec is 144.0 against a minimum_dwell_sec of 180 for LARGE_VENUE, giving a shortfall_sec of 36.0. The trace is clean — 100% coverage, 10 s cadence, no gaps, both tracks present — so the arithmetic is not in doubt.

The rider was at the pickup and actively coordinating. At 13:32:56, while the driver was inside the geofence, the rider sent 'im at the lobby, coming out'. The driver's only reply, 'ok', came at 13:33:11 — 15 seconds later — and the driver cancelled at 13:34:24, roughly 73 seconds after that reply. The rider's device track places the rider within 18.4 m of the pin throughout, well inside the 150 m rider presence radius for LARGE_VENUE, for all 45 qualifying fixes.

The driver's stated reason — 'Rider was not visible and I had another booking waiting' — is not one of the three reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises (RIDER_NO_SHOW, RIDER_UNREACHABLE, EXCESSIVE_WAIT). The trip record's cancellation_reason_code is RIDER_NO_SHOW, but the driver's own contemporaneous statement shows the real motive was a competing booking, not the rider's failure to appear. Limb (d) of the baseline chargeable no-show is therefore not satisfied on the driver's own account.

The rider's message 'im at the lobby, coming out' is a locating statement — it names the rider's position at the lobby. Under POL-NS-04(a) that is exactly the kind of coordinating message the clause contemplates, and it was sent during the waiting window. The driver's reply 'ok' does not cure the shortfall: POL-NS-04(b) is about whether the driver replied within 120 seconds, but the fee's chargeability turns on the dwell under POL-NS-06, which the reply cannot extend.

The fare breakdown shows the rider was charged SGD 4.50 as a cancellation fee, with payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. The amount contested is SGD 4.50. Under POL-NS-06 the cancellation-fee line is refunded in full; no booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip, so the full SGD 4.50 is the refund figure.

No traffic advisory covers this pickup. EV-ADVIS-02707-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so the driver cannot invoke POL-NS-06(i) to accumulate dwell across separate in-geofence intervals — and in any event the trace shows only one in-geofence interval (run_count 1), so there is no second interval to sum. The 36-second shortfall stands unmitigated.

The driver's profile shows no_show_terminations_30d of 0 and completed_trips_30d of 54, so the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip and no escalation is warranted on that ground. The rider's profile shows no_show_disputes_30d of 1 and disputes_with_counterparty_90d of 0 on both sides, so POL-NS-09(c) and (d) are not engaged. The case is decidable on the arithmetic alone.

claims.text: The driver's own trace places him inside the LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for a continuous qualifying run of 144 seconds, from 13:31:56 to 13:34:20, and the trip record's 'arrived' event timestamp (13:31:56) matches the first qualifying in-geofence fix exactly, so POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied on the driver's own evidence.

The driver terminated the trip at 13:34:24 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, which is one of the three reason codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, and no boarding event is recorded, so limb (d) is satisfied.

The rider's own device track places the rider within 18.4 m of the pickup pin throughout the waiting window (45 fixes, all stationary, max distance 18.39 m), well inside the 150 m rider-presence radius for LARGE_VENUE, so the rider was at the pin and the driver's inability to see him is not a mislocation case under POL-NS-03.

The rider's chat message 'im at the lobby, coming out' was sent at 13:32:56 and the driver replied 'ok' at 13:33:11, within 120 seconds, so POL-NS-04 limb (b) fails and the rider-exonerating clause does not apply; the driver did respond.

The rider's message itself concedes he was still inside the building ('coming out') at 13:32:56, 88 seconds after the driver's arrival at 13:31:56, and the driver cancelled 88 seconds later at 13:34:24; the rider was not at the kerb when the driver arrived.

The fare breakdown shows the cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 was charged and payment_status is CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00, so the present state is that the rider has paid and the driver has not been compensated; NO_ACTION on this rider-filed dispute leaves that charge standing, which is the driver's win on the fee.

The driver's anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 does not trip: no_show_terminations_30d is 0, which is below the 4-or-more threshold, and 0 divided by completed_trips_30d (54) is 0.00, below the 0.08 rate threshold, so compensation is payable and the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION at 80 percent of the SGD 4.50 fee, i.e. SGD 3.60.

The rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below the 3-or-more threshold in POL-NS-09(d), and the parties have 0 disputes_with_counterparty_90d each, so neither escalation trigger (c) nor (d) fires and the case does not need human review on those grounds.

The traffic advisory artifact EV-ADVIS-02707-01 is MISSING with weight 0.0, so POL-NS-06(i) cannot be run to accumulate dwell across intervals; but the driver's single qualifying run of 144 seconds is the only in-geofence interval, and the shortfall of 36 seconds against the 180-second free waiting period is the rider's strongest point, which I do not contest on the arithmetic.

The driver's arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: the trip record's 'arrived' event at 13:31:56 matches the first qualifying in-geofence fix at 13:31:56, and the driver's speed at that fix is 0.0 kph, well below the 15 kph motion threshold, so the waiting clock was not started early.

The driver's stationary fixes are inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, not outside it, so POL-NS-03 (wrong-entrance) does not govern and the driver is not claiming the 400 m wrong-face-of-venue route; the case is decided under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-07.

ruling.explanation:
Rider — you get the SGD 4.50 back. Driver — the fee does not stand, but not because anyone acted in bad faith.

The timeline is common ground. The trip record shows you arrived at Northpoint City at 13:31:56 and terminated the trip at 13:34:24 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW. The GPS trace puts you inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE pickup geofence from 13:31:56 — the first qualifying in-geofence fix matches your arrival marker exactly, with speed 0.0 km/h — and you held position until 13:34:20. That is 144 seconds of continuous in-geofence dwell; the derived arrival block reports the same figures (longest_run_sec 144.0; run_count 1; shortfall_sec 36.0).

The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec; fee_schedule.defaults agrees). POL-NS-01 limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 180 seconds, measured from the first qualifying fix. 144 seconds is 36 seconds short, so limb (c) fails and the baseline charge cannot stand. Limb (d) is also short on timing: the cancellation at 13:34:24 came about 32 seconds before the 180-second dwell would have run out at 13:34:56. POL-NS-06 then applies directly: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded. The amount refunded is the SGD 4.50 cancellation-fee line (fare_breakdown.cancellation_fee 4.50; total_charged 4.50; payment_status CHARGED; refund_issued_sgd 0.00). No booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-06 withholds it on a shortfall, and POL-NS-07's payout engages only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full — which it is not.

On the claims. For the driver: the points that POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied (arrived event present; first qualifying in-geofence fix coinciding with it) and that limb (d)'s reason code is RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three recognised codes, are accepted as facts — but the fee still fails on limb (c), and the cancellation preceded the dwell completing. The POL-NS-04 point is accepted: the driver did reply 'ok' at 13:33:11, 15 seconds after the rider's 13:32:56 message, so the rider-contact clause does not exonerate the rider; that simply leaves the case where POL-NS-06 already puts it. The description of the present state (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00) is accurate, but NO_ACTION is rejected as the outcome: POL-NS-06 licenses FULL_REFUND. The claim for DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 3.60 (80 percent of 4.50) is rejected, because POL-NS-07 pays only on a fee that stands. The points that the arrival marker is not false (inside the radius, stationary at the arrival timestamp, so POL-NS-05 is not engaged) and that POL-NS-03 does not govern are accepted, and no false-arrival referral arises.

For the rider: the POL-NS-06 arithmetic is accepted and decides the case. The POL-NS-04 point is accepted as to the message being a locating statement ('im at the lobby, coming out'), and the rider track does place the device within about 18.4 m of the pin across all 45 fixes — but POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate because the driver replied within 120 seconds, so the refund comes from POL-NS-06, not that clause. The SGD 4.50 figure is accepted. The argument that limb (d) fails because the driver's statement ('I had another booking waiting') shows a motive other than the rider's failure to appear is rejected: POL-NS-01(d) reads the trip_record's cancellation_reason_code, which is RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three recognised codes, and the driver's separate statement is not one of that limb's tests; in any event the fee already fails on limb (c), so nothing turns on it.

Impairment and weight. Nothing the ruling rests on is impaired: the trip record, GPS trace, chat log and fare breakdown all carry weight_multiplier 1.0 with no issues, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-02707-01) is MISSING at weight 0.0 with issue MISSING_ARTIFACT, but it is not relied on: it bears only on POL-NS-06(i), which would let separate in-geofence intervals be summed, and the trace shows a single interval (run_count 1). Two claims built on that missing artifact were discarded by the citation referee for not naming its issue code; that has no effect on the outcome.

Escalation and execution. Confidence is above the 0.70 floor, so POL-NS-09(a) is not engaged; there is no direct contradiction between admissible artifacts on arrival, dwell or rider presence (b); the parties show no repeat disputes (c); the anti-farming check does not trip (0 no-show terminations in 30 days against 54 completed trips) and the rider's no_show_disputes_30d is 1 (d); and the deciding fact is carried by unimpaired evidence (e). The SGD 4.50 refund is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05 and executes on issue, subject to the appeal route under POL-GEN-04.

ruling.explanation:
Ruling for the rider. The disputed charge is the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee on trip TRP-02707, which the driver cancelled at 13:34:24 with reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW.

What the record shows. The driver's arrival marker is at 13:31:56 (trip record), and the GPS trace places the driver inside the Northpoint City pickup geofence from 13:31:56 to 13:34:20 — one continuous qualifying run of 144 seconds (EV-GPS-02707, derived arrival block: longest_run_sec 144.0, run_count 1). The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds (trip_record.platform_policy.free_wait_sec). The driver cancelled 36 seconds short of it.

Why the fee does not stand. POL-NS-01(c) requires the driver to hold position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least 180 seconds, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix, not from any later tap. 144 seconds does not meet it. Limb (d) also fails: the trip had to be terminated at or after the moment the required dwell elapsed, which is 13:34:56; it was terminated at 13:34:24. POL-NS-06 therefore applies: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full. POL-NS-06(i) cannot rescue the dwell — it needs a present and populated traffic advisory of type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT, and the derived arrival block records limb (i) as unavailable on this record (no advisory and only one in-geofence interval, so there is no second interval to sum).

The driver's points. Limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied — the 'arrived' event at 13:31:56 matches the first qualifying in-geofence fix — and the arrival marker is not false under POL-NS-05: the marker matches the in-geofence fix and the driver's speed there is 0.0 kph, far below the 15 kph motion test, so the waiting clock correctly ran from 13:31:56. The fixes lie inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, so POL-NS-03 (wrong-entrance) does not govern. None of this, however, cures limb (c). The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d 0 against 54 completed trips in 30 days), but POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, which it is not; so the driver's claim that the charge should stand (NO_ACTION) is not accepted, and the SGD 3.60 he seeks (80 percent of SGD 4.50) is not payable. The rider being within 18.4 m of the pin is accepted and merely confirms this is not a mislocation case; the driver's observation that the rider's own message ('im at the lobby, coming out') shows him still inside the building at 13:32:56 is also accepted, but POL-NS-06 refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present, so it does not change the outcome.

The rider's points. The 144-second dwell against the 180-second minimum, stated from the derived block with its 36-second shortfall, is accepted and decides the case. His POL-NS-04 argument does not itself carry him: he did send a locating message at 13:32:56, but the driver replied 'ok' 15 seconds later, so limb (b) fails and that clause does not apply — he does not need it. His point that the driver's statement ('I had another booking waiting') defeats limb (d) is noted: limb (d) reads the trip record's reason code, which is RIDER_NO_SHOW, a code the clause recognises, so the code is not itself mis-selected; and limb (d) fails in any event on timing for the reason given above.

Amount. The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-02707) shows a cancellation fee of SGD 4.50, payment_status CHARGED and refund_issued_sgd 0.00. No booking or platform fee was charged on this cancelled trip, so there is nothing beyond the SGD 4.50 to refund. The rider receives the full SGD 4.50; driver_compensation_sgd is null.

Confidence. The deciding fact — the 144-second dwell against the 180-second free waiting period — is carried by EV-GPS-02707 and EV-TRIP-02707, both at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0 and the finding is well above the 0.70 escalation floor. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: the artifacts do not contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the profiles show no trailing-90-day counterparty pattern and no_show_disputes_30d is 1; and the deciding evidence is not impaired.

Execution and appeal. The monetary effect of SGD 4.50 is below the POL-GEN-05 execution threshold of SGD 8.00, so it executes automatically on issue. This is a provisional ruling made without human review; either party may appeal once within 30 days under POL-GEN-04.

This ruling is addressed to both parties.

WHAT HAPPENED. The trip was accepted at 13:26:38. The driver pressed 'arrived' at 13:31:56, and the GPS trace (EV-GPS-02707) places his vehicle inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius from 13:31:56 to 13:34:20 — a single continuous qualifying run of 144 seconds. He cancelled at 13:34:24 recording RIDER_NO_SHOW. The rider's message at 13:32:56 read 'im at the lobby, coming out' and the driver replied 'ok' at 13:33:11.

THE DECIDING ARITHMETIC. The free waiting period in force for this trip is 180 seconds, read from the trip record's own platform_policy.free_wait_sec (EV-TRIP-02707); the SGD 4.50 cancellation fee is likewise read from that record and reconciles with the fare breakdown line (EV-FARE-02707). POL-NS-01(c) makes the fee chargeable only if the driver held position inside the geofence for a continuous dwell of at least that 180-second period. The measured dwell is 144 seconds, a shortfall of 36 seconds (the derived arrival block states the same figures: longest_run_sec 144.0 against minimum_dwell_sec 180). Limb (c) therefore fails, and the fee is not chargeable. POL-NS-06 then applies directly: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the free waiting period, the cancellation fee is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages.

THE DRIVER'S POINTS. (1) Arrival is established — limbs (a) and (b) are satisfied — and the driver is right that the 'arrived' marker at 13:31:56 is not a false marker under POL-NS-05 (the driver's speed at that fix is 0.0 kph and he is in-geofence, not the 300 m or 15 kph trigger), so the waiting clock was not started early. (2) The recorded reason code RIDER_NO_SHOW is one of the three codes POL-NS-01(d) recognises, so limb (d) is satisfied on the record; the Rider Advocate's argument that the driver's separate statement ('I had another booking waiting') mis-selects the reason code is rejected — the code the platform recorded is a recognised one, and a party's narrative does not overwrite the record field. (3) POL-NS-03 (wrong-entrance) does not govern: the stationary fixes lie inside the 120 m radius, not outside it within 400 m. (4) The driver's request for payout under POL-NS-07 is refused because POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not: one limb fails. The anti-farming check itself does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d is 0, below the 4-or-more threshold), but that check only gates a compensation that has already become payable, and none is.

THE RIDER'S POINTS. POL-NS-06 is accepted and is the ground of the ruling. The rider's presence within 18.4 m of the pin on 45 clean fixes is noted but makes no difference to the fee under POL-NS-06. POL-NS-04 does not apply in the rider's favour either: limb (b) requires that the driver did not reply within 120 seconds of the rider's message, and the driver replied 'ok' 15 seconds later, so that clause cannot be used — though the outcome is the same through POL-NS-06.

EVIDENCE AND CONFIDENCE. Both artifacts carrying the deciding fact — the GPS trace and the trip record — carry weight_multiplier 1.0, and the trace is clean (100% coverage, 10 s cadence, no gaps, both tracks present); the fare line reconciles to the net fee and the chat log matches the recorded message count of 2. No integrity defect under POL-NS-08(a)-(d) exists and no POL-NS-09 escalation trigger fires (confidence is not below 0.70; there is no direct artifact contradiction; counterparty disputes are 0 on both sides; rider no_show_disputes_30d is 1, below 3; no sole impaired evidence). The 0.36-second margin of comfort is irrelevant — the shortfall is 36 full seconds.

ORDER. The cancellation fee of SGD 4.50 is refunded in full to the rider. No driver compensation is payable (the fee was premature). The refund (SGD 4.50) is below the SGD 8.00 automatic-execution threshold in POL-GEN-05, so it executes on issue subject to the appeal route in POL-GEN-04. No referral is issued: no clause in this category produces one on these facts (the arrival marker was not false under POL-NS-05, the reason code was not mis-selected, and the anti-farming check did not trip).

The driver's stationary fixes are inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, not outside it, so POL-NS-03 (wrong-entrance) does not govern and the driver is not claiming the 400 m wrong-face-of-venue route; the case is decided under POL-NS-01 and POL-NS-07.
